ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory automated screening of all UBOs, directors, shareholders and authorized signatories against the UN Security Council Consolidated List (OFSI/UNSC 1267/1988), OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK OFSI Consolidated List, Egyptian EMLTFCU local terrorist list, and Interpol notices. Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) is mandatory for any person meeting the FATF politically exposed person (PEP) definition or convicted of financial crimes; all matters are escalated to anti-fraud officer and the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit if any positive hit is identified.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI Electronic Companies' Registry via the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones portal (www.gafi.gov.eg)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be stated in Arabic script; a Latin-script transliteration may be registered alongside the Arabic name. The Arabic name must not conflict with an existing trade name, mark, or the name of a public authority, and must comply with Arabic naming conventions and social decency standards.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Militarized terms or names of armed forces
Any token implying a scope not present in the memorandum of association
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the GAFI Name Clearance Committee within 15 business days, stating the reasons for disputing the rejection. The Committee shall issue a decision within 30 business days. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may initiate a second administrative remedy before the GAFI Legal Affairs Department, followed by judicial review before the competent Administrative Court of Egypt under Law No. 119 of 2008.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office services are not acceptable for the regulated Multi-Family Office / Discretionary Portfolio Advisory license (ISIC 6430); the entity must maintain a physical registered office and licensed operational premises in Egypt that host at least one licensed resident compliance officer and allow on-site reviews by the Financial Regulatory Authority and the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High — 92% within the first 12 months of registration, with rights of unannounced on-site inspections under Article 21 of Law No. 80 of 2002 and Banking Law No. 194 of 2020.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 194 of 2020, Articles 7-8 and 22-31 (Limited Liability Company formation, memorandum and articles of association), read together with Executive Regulations (Prime Ministerial Decree No. 1590 of 2020)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) — Company Registration and One-Stop-Shop Departments
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: GAFI Incorporation Application Form (Form 1) together with the notarized Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association, filed in the Commercial Registry
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for LLCs under Law No. 194 of 2020; the issued capital must be fully subscribed and paid into a temporary escrow account at a licensed Egyptian bank, with a provisional deposit certificate lodged with GAFI and released only upon issuance of the certificate of incorporation. For the family-office activity, an FRA sectoral license additionally applies a regulatory minimum paid-in capital (approximately US$100,000) with a permanent bank deposit certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: (1) the incorporators' subscription of the issued share capital of [Company] LLC, comprising [•] ordinary shares of EGP [•] each, is approved and ratified; (2) the registered office is established at [address, Cairo], where the company seal, financial books, and statutory registers shall be kept; (3) [Name] is appointed CEO/Manager, [Name] CFO, and [Name] Corporate Secretary, each for a term ending at the next annual meeting, with authority to open bank accounts and execute regulatory filings; (4) management is directed to complete all post-incorporation registrations with GAFI, the Financial Regulatory Authority, and the tax and social-insurance authorities, and to obtain the sectoral license required for discretionary portfolio advisory services.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Pre-Approval at GAFI One-Stop Shop
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop (Cairo headquarters or governorate branch); online submission via the GAFI 'Invest in Egypt' portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit five ranked proposals for the Arabic and English trade names, together with the founders' identity documents and a statement of corporate object. GAFI checks each name against the Commercial Registry index, reserved or owned names, and public order. Once approved, obtain the official name-reservation certificate valid for 60 days.
required_dossiers: Passport or national ID copies of all founding shareholders
Power of attorney if submission is made through a proxy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file an administrative objection to the GAFI Naming Committee within 15 days, or substitute new names; correction normally cures the application within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Escrow Deposit of Share Capital and Provisional Bank Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any licensed Egyptian commercial bank operating an escrow and capital-certificate desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary escrow account in the formation name; each founder transfers their allotted share capital contribution in Egyptian pounds. Upon full payment, obtain an escrow certificate and a provisional deposit receipt reflecting the paid-up capital. The funds remain blocked until GAFI issues the certificate of incorporation and are unconditionally released only after commercial registration.
required_dossiers: Copy of the draft memorandum of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the deposit is rejected for KYC reasons, re-submit corrected ownership and source-of-funds declarations and escalate to the bank compliance officer for re-review within 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Notary Public Authority branches or GAFI-attached notary windows
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge the executed Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association with certified passport copies, the name certificate, and the escrow receipt. Each founder signs in person before the notary; corporate shareholders must produce authenticated corporate resolutions. The notary issues the officially notarized copy and enrolls the instrument in the notarial roll.
required_dossiers: Signed Memorandum and Articles of Association in Arabic
Passports or national IDs of all signatories
Corporate authorizations for any corporate shareholders
Tax ID or national ID of the proposed manager(s)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises a query on document inconsistencies, execute a notarial correction memorandum; re-attestation is normally granted within 3 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI Incorporation Filing and Commercial Registry Entry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit GAFI Form 1, the notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association, the escrow certificate, the name certificate, and signed appointment letters for managers and authorized officers. Pay the incorporation and registry fees. GAFI issues the certificate of incorporation and enrolls the company in the Commercial Registry; obtain the commercial registration number, official extract, and the company seal into the official register.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Registered office lease or address proof
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a query (e.g., capital description mismatch or overly broad corporate object), respond in writing within the 30-day cure period; revise the object or capital schedule and re-file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Governance, Tax and Social Insurance Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI), Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS), and GAFI post-registration window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, convene the first board of managers to adopt the pro-forma board resolution; issue share certificates; open a permanent corporate bank account at a licensed bank; submit tax registration Form 8; register for corporate income tax, VAT, and payroll; register managers and employees for social insurance; obtain the tax card and statistical card; authenticate all corporate books and the Commercial Registry extract.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late or missing tax registration attracts an administrative fine; file a remedial application to ETA with a notarized representation and settle the fine; NOSI accepts retroactive registration upon penalty payment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) — Capital Markets Licensing Department
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Portfolio Management (Multi-Family Office Discretionary Advisory) License for Non-Banking Financial Services under the Egyptian Capital Market Law No. 95 of 1992 and the FRA Executive Regulations, as amended

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) — Ministry of Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: White List (Category C) — Registration/Exempt: office-based financial services with no significant industrial pollution; a simplified environmental registration form suffices and no full EIA Report is required under Law No. 4 of 1994 on the Environment, as amended by Law No. 9 of 2009
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Office wastewater discharge to public sewer must comply with Prime Ministerial Decree No. 44 of 2000 (Code 001 standards); no VOC-emitting industrial processes; electronic records archiving to minimize paper waste; any discarded confidential client records must be handled by a licensed waste contractor under EEAA waste-management rules and Law No. 4 of 1994.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Civil Defense Authority fire-safety clearance for the occupied office floor, including verified evacuation plans, fire-extinguishing equipment, and a building-level civil defense certificate; structural load inspection certificate from a licensed engineer confirming office-floor loading capacity of at least 300 kgf/m² for the financial records vault; Ministry of Manpower workplace clearance under Labor Law No. 12 of 2003, covering fire exits, minimum safety measures, and employee occupational health cards.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance; unified e-services portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg; mandatory e-invoicing/e-receipts platform: https://invoicing.eta.gov.eg.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned Egyptian LLC, the manager must first obtain incorporation certificate from GAFI and the Commercial Register (no statutory minimum capital). The MFO must also hold its FRA capital-markets concession before commencing activity. Within 30 days of commercial registration the entity files with ETA for a Tax Card (unified TIN) providing the notarized memorandum of association, commercial registration, premises lease, board resolution, beneficial-owner declarations and director identity papers. VAT registration under VAT Law 67/2016 is separate: registration is compulsory when taxable supplies reach EGP 500,000 per annum, or earlier when the company intends to claim input VAT credits, export zero-rating, or import with VAT deferral; the VAT ID is stamped onto the same Tax Card. A non-resident without an Egyptian branch must appoint a resident fiscal representative jointly and severally liable. Final step: activation of the ETA e-invoice account and API integration for billing software.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: Egyptian LLC is a tax-resident legal person subject to corporate income tax on worldwide profits at the standard CIT rate of 22.5% under Law 91/2005; no pass-through treatment exists.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch pass-through election is available; LLC treatment is mandatory under Egyptian law. Permitted elections are limited to: (i) voluntary VAT registration below the EGP 500,000 threshold; (ii) election to classify designated service contracts as exported services for 0% VAT; (iii) for licensed projects, election to operate under a General Free Zone or Suez Canal Economic Zone regime (annual fee in lieu of customs/VAT; 0% CIT on export profits); (iv) treaty-based relief elections for foreign investors; (v) irrevocable e-invoicing integration go-live elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) — Law No. 67 of 2016 and Executive Regulations, as amended.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 aggregate annual value of taxable supplies; importers are also liable to register from the first import, regardless of turnover. Voluntary registration is allowed below the threshold, mainly to recover input VAT and support export zero-rating.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT registrants must integrate their billing systems with ETA REST APIs and transmit each B2B invoice in the ETA XML/JSON schema (UBL 2.1-aligned, Arabic-first) at the moment of issuance for real-time centralized validation. ETA assigns a unique invoice identifier and digitally stamps the invoice with an RSA-SHA256 QR code (ISO/IEC 18004); the seller must render that QR stamp on the invoice copy sent to the buyer. An invoice without an ETA-validated code is legally non-compliant and cannot support input VAT deduction or zero-rating. E-receipts are mandatory for B2C transactions; customs and banking records are automatically reconciled with the e-invoice dataset.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods are zero-rated under VAT Law Art. 26(1) when physically exported outside Egypt within the timeframe fixed in the Executive Regulations and in any event within the CBE's 180-day FX-repatriation window, supported by customs release and conversion of proceeds in convertible currency through an Egyptian bank. Services are zero-rated under Art. 26(2) when supplied to a non-resident recipient for use and performance wholly outside Egypt, paid from abroad in foreign currency through the Egyptian banking system. For this domestic-licensed MFO, only genuinely offshore discretionary advisory mandates meeting those tests qualify as exported services; portfolio management and custody provided to resident or non-resident clients within Egypt fall under the VAT-exempt financial-services list, which suppresses output VAT and blocks input VAT recovery.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: ETA-matched Customs Export Declaration (Egyptian customs port release/exit statement) reflecting exact invoice value and tariff classification
Original negotiable Bill of Lading, Air Waybill or CMR border export document naming the Egyptian LLC as consignor with Egypt as origin

Bank-issued Inward Remittance Certificate / Foreign-Currency Proceeds Certificate evidencing full consideration credited to the LLC's Egyptian bank account within the statutory 180-day repatriation deadline
Commercial export invoice and packing list in the ETA e-invoice format carrying the ETA-validated QR code and the statutory zero-rating export clause
Executed international sale contract or advisory engagement agreement setting out Incoterms for goods, or the performance location and non-Egyptian utilization clauses for offshore services

For offshore MFO services: SWIFT interbank credit evidence (Custody_Wire rail), updated KYC and beneficial-ownership file of the non-resident client, engagement/portfolio advisory mandates, and minutes or digital records proving delivery outside Egyptian territory
Copy of the ETA zero-rating request/acknowledgment and import-export registration file where the exporter was required to obtain prior approval of the export classification
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ETA automatically reconciles every zero-rated e-invoice against customs export declarations, bank FX-receipt records and corporate e-filings; credit is withdrawn if the export window is missed, proceeds are not repatriated within 180 days, documents are falsified, or the service is found to be consumed in Egypt. Fraudulent claims trigger immediate clawback of the VAT refund, reassessment at 14% VAT with statutory late-payment surcharges, and the evasion penalties of VAT Law 67/2016 (imprisonment of up to 5 years and fines). Repeated or organized falsification leads to suspension of the ETA e-invoice clearance account, blacklisting in the Customs risk engine, and referrals for money-laundering scrutiny under AML Law 80/2002.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) as the principal exchange-control authority, acting jointly with the General Authority for Investment (GAFI) on inbound capital registration and with the Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) on portfolio-advisory licensing of the Multi-Family Office; the Egyptian Money Laundering Combating Unit (EMLCU) performs AML/CFT pre-clearance and suspicious-transaction oversight for the High_Risk_Special_License entity.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt operates a managed-floating EGP with full current-account convertibility for genuine trade, services, dividends, and interest remittances, subject to documentary checks at CBE-licensed banks; the capital account remains partially convertible and every inbound equity or shareholder-loan injection must pass source-of-funds verification, GAFI company-registry capitalization, and CBE balance-of-payments purpose-code classification. Profit-remittance hurdles include: (i) an electronic tax-clearance certificate demonstrating settled corporate income tax, VAT, and stamp duties; (ii) bank-level review lasting five to ten business days triggered by the ISIC 6430 high-risk financial classification; (iii) exact beneficiary matching in MT103 field 59 and Remittance Information field 72; and (iv) the periodic scarcity of USD/EUR interbank liquidity, during which the CBE priorities framework may defer discretionary outbound foreign-currency transfers. EGP is not deeply deliverable offshore, so hedgeable foreign exchange is concentrated in onshore forwards, FX swaps, and offshore NDF reference pricing.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: CBE Foreign Exchange Regulations require 100% of goods or service export proceeds to enter Egypt through a licensed domestic bank: the statutory repatriation window is 7 business days from the maturity/due date of the collection document and in all cases no later than 30 calendar days from the bill-of-lading date for goods, or 30 days from the invoice due date for services and advisory fees. The mandatory conversion/surrender ratio to EGP is 0% after the November 2016 exchange-rate liberalization, meaning the exporter or the Multy-Family Office receiving service fees may credit export receipts to a foreign-currency account without forced conversion to EGP, but the receiving bank must report the proceeds to the CBE within 7 working days of credit. Failure to repatriate within the timeline triggers penalty interest, denial of new import facilities, and liabilities under Law No. 194 of 1980 as amended by Law No. 80 of 2015.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of Alexandria S.A.E. (Intesa Sanpaolo Group)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low as a primary domestic clearing host; Medium as a foreign-currency staging corridor. Egypt's Payment Systems Law No. 18 of 2019 and the CBE non-bank licensing regime reserve the interbank clearing rails (EGYPS/RTGS and instant payment systems) to CBE-licensed banks and licensed fintechs admitted to the CBE Regulatory Sandbox. Offshore EMIs, including FCA-regulated UK EMIs and EU PSD2 payment institutions, cannot hold EGP-denominated client floats, cannot onboard Egyptian residents as local payment-account holders, and must not be presented as the host bank of the EG_LLC in any CBE filing. The permissible use is limited to collecting non-EGP family subscriptions under custody wrappers and initiating SWIFT transfers to the onshore escrow account; the EMI must not serve as clearing counterparty for the Egyptian entity's domestic operating expenses.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person onboarding is mandatory: the two authorized directors, the designated compliance officer, and the ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) of the EG_LLC must appear before the relationship manager at an Egyptian bank branch in Cairo or at a CBE-licensed alternative presence for biometric identity verification. Remote or video-only account opening is not available to non-resident directors of a High_Risk_Special_License financial entity; e-KYC is reserved for Egyptian tax-resident natural persons and smaller commercial corporates under CBE fintech guidance. Consular notarization and powers of attorney remain admissible for administrative steps but do not override the bank's right, and in most banks the unconditional legal requirement, to retrieve an in-person interview with at least one authorized natural-person director/UBO before signatory authority is activated.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: operating under ISIC 6430 as a Discretionary Multi-Family Office without an immediately verifiable special license, exposing the bank to unlicensed wealth-management counterparty risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Regulatory bundle: GAFI certificate of incorporation and updated commercial registry extract; FRA non-bank financial activity license for portfolio management, or an official exemption letter for the family office structure; CBE No-Objection Letter where the entity holds client money; AML/CFT compliance manual and independent audit opinion; board resolution appointing the compliance officer; professional indemnity policy and evidence of regulatory capital or net-worth adequacy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: layered or partially disclosed UBO cascade with foreign settlor family members exceeding the 25% ownership threshold in a higher-risk jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete UBO schedule with chain-of-title registry extracts for the Egyptian LLC; certified company registry extracts and shareholder registers; tax-residence certificates for every UBO; family wealth-origin statements supported by audited financials, sale contracts, inheritance apportionments, and dividend vouchers; independent Egyptian counsel legal opinion confirming no hidden principals under Companies Law No. 159 of 2020.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: repeated third-party 'settlement instruction' wires and custody transfers to counterparties outside the nominal mandate of a family-office entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed discretionary portfolio mandate agreements for each private family; pre-approved counterparty distribution list; shadow ledger reconciling custody wires and Swift interbank movements; FATCA and CRS self-certification for each beneficiary; negative sanctions-screening results across OFAC, UN, EU, UK, and CBE domestic lists; maker-checker dual-approval authorization matrix for all outbound transfers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: high-frequency offshore cross-border flows suggesting circumvention of the Egyptian banking channel or unlicensed remittance arrangements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Professional legal opinion confirming the MFO does not operate an unlicensed payment or remittance business; evidence of Egyptian economic substance including leased office, local payroll, CBE bank-account presence, and Cairo-domiciled signatories; sworn representation that no offshore re-denomination of EGP receivables and no loan-back structures are used; annual audited statements demonstrating that flows are investment-transactional and tax-disclosed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: politically exposed person (PEP) status of a participating family principal or politically connected beneficiary of the discretionary mandates.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced Due Diligence file with independent PEP risk assessment; source-of-wealth evidence excluding public-sector funding origins; signed undertaking to notify the EMLCU of any transaction above the statutory declaration threshold; external audit opinion confirming the ADB-grade compliance infrastructure of the family office; written risk mitigation and monitoring plan for the bank's AML/CFT committee.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contributions and family subscriptions must be wired into a Capital Escrow Account at a CBE-licensed Egyptian bank using SWIFT MT103 for customer credit or MT202 COV for bank-for-own-account transfers, in freely convertible currencies (USD, EUR, GBP), with Remittance Information in field 70 stating 'INVESTMENT CAPITAL INCREASE — EG_LLC — GAFI FILE REF 6430-MFO — BoP Purpose Code 3.2.1 Capital Contribution'; the originating institution must supply source-of-funds evidence, and the receiving Egyptian bank must classify the transfer under the CBE unified transfer-purpose framework within two business days, verify the beneficiary name alignment, and record the capitalization in the GAFI commercial registry; USD-clearing is executed through the Egyptian bank's New York correspondent (BNY Mellon or JPMorgan) under OFAC screening; cash deposits, precious metals, crypto-assets, dual-switch round-trips, and third-party spontaneous donations are prohibited from use as capital-injection instruments.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for treasury and trade settlements: SWIFT MT103 customer credits for custody fees and family-level disbursements, with MT202 for interbank positioning; EGP legs are settled through the Egyptian RTGS/EGYPS network; USD, EUR, and GBP outbound flows are routed via CIB or HSBC Egypt correspondent networks, respectively CHIPS/Fedwire in New York, TARGET2 in Europe, and CHAPS in London; documentary trade settlements are structured as Commercial Letters of Credit under UCP600, opened or confirmed by the Egyptian account bank, with the Multi-Family Office acting only as instructing principal on documented client transactions and never as a merchant acquiring settlement house; each outbound disbursement must carry the exact purpose code, a definite beneficiary matching the underlying mandate, and, for amounts above CBE thresholds, an ex-ante economic-substance or no-capital-flight certification issued by the account bank.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable onshore FX forward contracts (USD/EGP and EUR/EGP) executed through a CBE-licensed counterparty bank with verified underlying investment or trade exposure and a tenor aligned to the bank's prudential limits

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) structures referencing the central EGP parity, admitted only as back-to-back hedges on foreign-currency receivables where the local leg settles via the Egyptian correspondent account and no synthetic EGP credit element is created
FX swaps and cross-currency swaps (CCS) in USD and EUR against EGP for structural hedging of the MFO invested capital, subject to CBE notification and prudential counterparty limits
Plain vanilla European FX options (call/put on EGP against USD/EUR) acquired for hedging and cash-yield smoothing, with premium invoices evidenced to the Egyptian tax authority

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Legal Persons)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months of fiscal year-end; 30 April for calendar-year companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 2% of tax due per month (maximum 18%); delay interest of 2% per month on unpaid tax; criminal fine up to EGP 50,000; director personal liability for unpaid corporate tax

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Audited Financial Statements Package (financial statements, manager's report, auditor's report, annual partners' meeting minutes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry, General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of fiscal year-end; 30 June for calendar-year companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of EGP 1,000 to EGP 10,000 under Companies Law 159/1981; suspension of commercial registration; administrative strike-off after continued non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry (GAFI); Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) for licensed MFO entities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually with the audited financial statements deposit; any shareholding or control change filed within 30 days of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine up to EGP 1,000,000 under AML Law 80/2002 (as amended); commercial registry strike-off; disqualification of managers

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: FRA Capital Market License Annual Renewal and Regulatory Dossier (audited financials, compliance report, net capital certificate)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA), Non-Banking Financial Activities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually before the license anniversary date; 31 March for calendar-year licensees
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Automatic license lapse; FRA fine of EGP 5,000 per month of delay; license withdrawal and compulsory transfer of discretionary client portfolios

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual AML / Counter-Terrorist Financing Compliance Report (risk assessment, STR statistics, UBO reconfirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA); Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (MLTFCU)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of fiscal year-end; 31 January for calendar-year licensees
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines from EGP 100,000 to EGP 1,000,000; license suspension or revocation for licensed portfolio managers

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry, General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Every 5 years from the registration anniversary date; payment due within 30 days before expiry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registration suspension 30 days after expiry; administrative strike-off of the entity; bar on new commercial registrations for defaulting managers

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Companies Law 159/1981 and its Executive Regulations, an independent certified auditor is compulsory for LLCs with share capital exceeding EGP 50,000 or upon request of shareholders holding at least 20% of capital; FRA-licensed portfolio managers and multi-family offices are subject to an unconditional annual audit requirement regardless of size
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS) issued under Ministry of Finance Decree 110/2015, substantially converged with IFRS; FRA-licensed non-banking financial entities must additionally apply FRA accounting, net-capital and custody-reconciliation instructions

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: LLCs must maintain a beneficial ownership register under Companies Law 159/1981 (as amended by Law 4/2018) and AML Law 80/2002; UBOs are declared at incorporation, changes are filed within 30 days, and an annual UBO confirmation accompanies the annual financial statements deposit; FRA-licensed MFOs must repeat the confirmation in the annual AML compliance report

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 150–600 per annum (Cairo business district representative office or registered agent)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500–12,000 per annum (dependent on discretionary portfolio size, number of client mandates, and volume of custody transactions)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Egypt's Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 provides a 50% corporate tax reduction for projects established in priority governorates outside Cairo, Giza, and Alexandria, and for certain strategic sector activities; Free Zones and the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZONE) may grant partial or full tax holidays for productive, export-oriented entities. A Multi-Family Office performing discretionary portfolio advisory for private client families does not qualify as a strategic industrial or export activity and, absent a special economic-zone license, remains fully subject to the 22.5% headline CIT rate on all Egyptian-source profits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form No. 19 (Corporate Income Tax Return), filed exclusively through the Egyptian Tax Authority's (ETA) unified electronic tax portal (www.eta.gov.eg and the affiliated e-tax/e-services system), integrated with the mandatory e-invoicing and e-receipts regimes. The return is accompanied by audited IFRS/EGAAP financial statements, statutory tax reconciliation schedules, the transfer-pricing disclosure, and the withholding tax statement (Form 41).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual filing obligation; three equal quarterly advance tax installments must be remitted during the tax year (by end of months 3, 6, and 9) based on the immediately preceding year's taxable profit.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual return must be filed within 4 months following the end of the fiscal year (calendar-year taxpayers: on or before 30 April). Quarterly advance installments are due at month 3, month 6, and month 9 ends.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identity: legal name, Tax Identification Number (TIN), commercial registry number, registered head-office address, fiscal year start and end dates, and principal activity code (ISIC 6430 / Trusts, funds and similar financial entities; multi-family office discretionary advisory).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders must appoint and disclose a resident tax representative on the return; the FRA/CBE license number of the Egyptian MFO must be stated, otherwise the filing is rejected as incomplete and triggers an automatic audit flag.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenues: all operating income from retainer fees, discretionary portfolio management fees, performance-based advisory fees, custodian onboarding commissions, referral rebates, interest on operating cash, and foreign-source billings attributable to services performed in Egypt; must reconcile to audited books and e-invoice records.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Fees billed to non-resident UHNW families for advisory decisions taken and implemented in Egypt are Egyptian-source income and fully taxable; offshore client location does not exclude revenue from Form 19 gross receipts, and intercompany sub-advisory payments must be separately disclosed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating expenses: salaries, social insurance contributions, office rent, professional liability insurance, market-data and portfolio-software subscriptions, regulatory license fees, and local consultancy costs; add-backs for non-deductible items (distribution payments, client entertainment above legal threshold, disallowed provisions, non-statutory depreciation, and fines).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border expenditures (foreign sub-advisors, software licensing, market-data vendors) are deductible only if the Egyptian MFO discharged statutory withholding at 20% or invoked a reduced DTA rate through certified TRC forms; otherwise the payment is recharacterized as a non-deductible dividend subject to 10% WHT.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income before loss offset and statutory adjustments; includes full statutory accounting of Egyptian-source P&L, FX revaluation on operating balances, and any deemed-profit minimum assessment applied by the ETA where books are incomplete.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute exclusively on Egyptian statutory accounts in EGP; client custody assets, family investment portfolios, and client FX positions held for non-resident families are off-balance-sheet fiduciary positions and must not be consolidated with the MFO's operating taxable base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction of carried-forward tax losses: net operating losses from prior years, deductible within the statutory 5-year carryforward window, provided the same licensed activity continued and the losses were acknowledged on previously approved returns.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only Egyptian LLC losses are eligible; losses of a foreign parent, sister vehicle, or another jurisdiction cannot be consolidated. Changing the commercial model from advisory services to passive investment holding invalidates the loss carryforward.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Chargeable income after loss offset; application of the 22.5% corporate rate; recognition of any complementary investment-incentive reduction (if a special-zone or priority-governorate license exists); calculation of assessed corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: An unlicensed MFO cannot claim an investment-law rate reduction; where records are non-compliant, the ETA's deemed-profit method imposes a minimum taxable base irrespective of offshore cost allocations and group service markups.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prepayments and credits: quarterly advance installments, taxes withheld at source on local income, foreign tax credits, and withholding-tax credits under Form 41; final outturn is a balance payable to the ETA, a refund claim, or a carryforward certificate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The 10% dividend WHT on upstream distributions to foreign shareholders is final and must be credited at shareholder level; any refund requires an e-filed refund claim plus an original TRC before the statutory limitation period lapses.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts an administrative penalty of EGP 1,000 per month or fraction thereof (scalable by the ETA to a ceiling of EGP 50,000); late payment incurs a non-deductible delay surcharge of 2% per month on the unpaid tax, capped at 100% of the assessed amount; failure to comply with mandatory e-invoicing/e-receipts and Form 41 withholding disclosures draws separate fines and an automatic high-compliance-risk rating.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% final withholding tax on dividend distributions made by an Egyptian LLC to its shareholders under Law No. 91 of 2005; the WHT is final with no additional entity-level tax on distributions, and the LLC remains liable for withholding and remittance to the ETA.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief on dividends (typically 5%-15% depending on the treaty, e.g., 5% for a 10%+ corporate shareholder under several treaties, 10% for the UAE-Egypt and UK-Egypt treaties, 15% for portfolio investors): (1) obtain an original Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from the residence state covering the distribution year, legally translated and apostilled; (2) file Form 41 and the treaty-relief application electronically through the ETA portal before distribution or, if tax was already withheld, file a refund claim; (3) submit a beneficial-ownership declaration confirming that the shareholder is not a conduit or pass-through entity; (4) retain the Egyptian share register, board distribution minutes, and audited documentation evidencing economic substance. The ETA assesses beneficial ownership and substance under OECD principles before granting the reduced rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Egyptian WHT on gross interest, royalties, and management/service fees paid by an Egyptian resident to non-residents: 20%. Treaty-reduced rates are commonly available (e.g., interest 10%-15% under Egypt-UAE and Egypt-France treaties, 15% under the US-Egypt treaty; royalties 10%-20% depending on asset class, with US-Egypt at 15% and Germany-Egypt at 15%-20%). For the MFO, payments to offshore portfolio-software vendors, market-data providers, global custodians, and foreign sub-advisors must be screened contractually and must have treaty relief substantiated by TRC before reduced WHT is applied at source.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File is mandatory where aggregate related-party transactions (goods, services, intangibles, financial) exceed EGP 15,000,000 per tax year; Master File is mandatory where the multinational group's consolidated turnover exceeds EGP 1,000,000,000; Country-by-Country Reporting notification is triggered for groups with consolidated revenue above EGP 10,000,000,000. Even where thresholds are not met, the MFO must complete the transfer-pricing disclosure annex, retain contemporaneous benchmarking documentation, and file it with Form 19.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt has not enacted UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations, but substance discipline is enforced through: (i) the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) recharacterizing artificial or sham arrangements; (ii) OECD-aligned beneficial-ownership and permanent establishment tests applied by the ETA to all DTA relief and free-zone claims; (iii) CFC and branch rules; and (iv) sectoral licensing by the FRA and Central Bank of Egypt requiring physical premises, resident directors, risk and strategy committees meeting in Egypt, and a locally employed compliance staff. A shell Egyptian MFO with all decision-making offshore, no payroll, and no substantive local control will be denied treaty benefits, fully re-assessed on the advisory fee base, and exposed to license revocation and deemed-profit taxation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly understating discretionary management retainers, performance fees, custodian onboarding commissions, or FX gains on operating balances; issuing artificial invoices to related service companies to shift Egyptian-source profits offshore; destroying or concealing accounting books, e-invoices, and Form 19 backup records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law No. 91 of 2005: imprisonment of up to 5 years plus a fine of EGP 5,000 to EGP 50,000; the ETA recovers the full understated tax plus the 2%-per-month delay surcharge (capped at 100%), and the taxpayer's tax-clearance certificate is suspended, freezing all profit repatriation, banking clearances, and government transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the actual officer in charge are jointly and severally liable for the assessed tax, surcharges, and administrative fines; deliberate concealment triggers criminal prosecution, travel bans, seizure of personal accounts, and disqualification from managing licensed financial entities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the Egyptian LLC as a letterbox entity that invoices advisory fees while all strategic, risk, and portfolio decisions are taken outside Egypt; routing fees through a tax-haven or treaty-haven parent with no Egyptian premises, payroll, or local board minutes in order to harvest treaty rates on dividends and cross-border fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ETA recharacterizes the arrangement under the GAAR: denial of treaty relief, reclassification of the entire fee base as Egyptian-source income, statutory WHT assessment at 10%-20%, transfer-pricing adjustments, delay surcharges of 2% per month (capped at 100%), and revocation of any free-zone or SCZONE status obtained on fictitious productivity claims.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors signing treaty-relief and substance declarations face criminal liability for false attestations under Article 134 of Law 91 of 2005; the actual manager is personally exposed to civil restitution for off-shored fees re-sourced to Egypt, bank account freezes, and travel bans while the ETA's fraud investigation proceeds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating discretionary portfolio and custody advisory functions without the required FRA / Central Bank of Egypt license and capital adequacy approvals; failing to file Suspicious Transaction Reports for high-risk foreign PEP clients; commingling client custodial assets with the LLC operating account; accepting third-party 'loans' from non-resident sources to disguise client money flows and bypass AML controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Egypt's Anti-Money Laundering Law No. 80 of 2002: imprisonment of 3 to 7 years and fines of EGP 50,000 to EGP 1,000,000 for laundering-linked conduct; administrative sanctions of up to EGP 5,000,000 by the FRA; immediate license revocation, mandatory liquidation, and referral to the ETA for deemed-profit assessment on unexplained turnovers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Criminal prosecution of directors and the AML compliance officer; personal asset seizure, travel bans, revocation of 'fit and proper' status, and a 5-to-10-year prohibition from managing any financial, investment, or portfolio-advisory company in Egypt.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Reporting economic distributions to foreign shareholders as offshore 'loans'; paying dividends from an Egyptian LLC without withholding and remitting the 10% dividend WHT; wiring operating profits abroad under non-arm's-length shareholder loans structured solely to circumvent WHT registration and Form 41 obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ETA will apply debt-equity recharacterization, restating wired funds as dividends, and impose the 10% WHT plus the 2%-per-month delay surcharge (capped at 100% of the tax); administrative fines for non-filed Form 41 statements follow, and the tax-clearance certificate remains suspended until full settlement of principal, surcharges, and fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who ordered non-withheld distributions are jointly and severally liable for the unremitted WHT and penalties; if offshore routing documentation exists, criminal evasion charges attach personally; travel bans and personal asset execution are instruments available to the ETA's recovery unit.
